title: Booking Rules and the Delivery Fee for Delivery & Pickup Appointments
content:
These booking rules apply to every Delivery & Pickup Appointment. They set which orders may be booked, which fulfillment method may serve the order, the dates and windows that may be chosen, and how the delivery fee is fixed and billed.

## 1. Booking conditions

1.1 **Signed order.** An appointment is booked only for a purchase order whose status is contracted. The status is read from the system record of the purchase order the appointment is for.

1.2 **The method must serve the distance.**
- A home delivery method serves distances up to its service radius.
- Kestrel Enclosed White-Glove Delivery serves only orders in the purchase programs listed in its entry conditions: Kestrel Premium Certified and Kestrel Factory Certified.
- Kestrel Fly & Drive requires the buyer's residential ZIP to be at least the method's minimum one-way distance from the hub.

1.3 **Date and window.** The appointment date must meet all of the following:
- it is at least the method's minimum scheduling lead days after the purchase agreement signing date;
- it is no more than the method's maximum scheduling horizon days after the booking date;
- it falls on one of the method's appointment days;
- it does not fall on one of the method's holiday closures;
- the appointment uses one of the method's windows.

Both day counts are in calendar days. The lead runs from the signing date. The horizon runs from the date the booking is made. A date exactly the minimum lead after signing meets the lead, and a date exactly the maximum horizon after booking meets the horizon.

## 2. The delivery fee

2.1 **Definition.** The delivery fee is the method's base delivery fee, plus the method's per-mile fee multiplied by the number of miles by which the appointment's distance from the hub exceeds the method's included radius. That excess is zero when the distance is within the included radius. The resulting amount is then limited to the method's delivery fee cap: the fee is the lower of that sum and the cap. Finally the fee is rounded to the cent. The cap applies to the sum of the base fee and the per-mile charge, and the rounding is done once, on the capped amount.

2.2 **Exchange replacement.** For the replacement vehicle of an exchange, the delivery fee is zero when the method waives exchange delivery fees.

2.3 **When it is billed.** The delivery fee is billed once, when the appointment is booked, as a fee entry for the appointment date. Rebooking a missed appointment does not bill the delivery fee again.

2.4 **Which appointments can be billed.** Fees are billed only on an appointment whose status is scheduled or missed. This applies to every fee on an appointment. The status is read from the system record of that appointment.

| Appointment status | Fee may be billed on it |
|---|---|
| Scheduled | Yes |
| Missed | Yes |
| Dispatched | No |
| Completed | No |
| Refused | No |
| Cancelled | No |

## 3. Worked fee examples (hypothetical method figures)

Assume a hypothetical method with a base fee of $150.00, an included radius of 100 miles, a per-mile fee of $1.50 and a cap of $350.00.

| Distance from the hub | Miles beyond the included radius | Base fee plus per-mile charge | Compared with the $350.00 cap | Delivery fee |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 80 miles | 0 | $150.00 | below the cap | $150.00 |
| 100 miles | 0 | $150.00 | below the cap | $150.00 |
| 180 miles | 80 | $150.00 plus $120.00, totalling $270.00 | below the cap | $270.00 |
| 260 miles | 160 | $150.00 plus $240.00, totalling $390.00 | above the cap | $350.00 |

**Rounding** (same hypothetical base fee and cap, with a per-mile fee of $1.35). At a distance of 133.33 miles, the excess is 33.33 miles. The per-mile charge is 33.33 multiplied by $1.35, which is $44.9955, and adding the base fee gives $194.9955. That is below the cap, so it is rounded to the cent: **$195.00**.

**Exchange replacement** (same hypothetical method, which waives exchange delivery fees). The fee is $0.00 at any of the distances above.

## 4. Boundary cases for the date (hypothetical lead of 3 days, horizon of 14 days)

- **Lead.** Signed on day D: an appointment on day D plus 3 meets the lead, and one on day D plus 2 does not.
- **Horizon.** Booked on day B: an appointment on day B plus 14 is within the horizon, and one on day B plus 15 is not.
- **Day and window.** A date that meets both counts still has to be one of the method's appointment days, must not be a holiday closure, and the window must be one the method offers.
